questions.stem: Which part of the eye contains the light-sensitive receptor cells?
questions.explanation: The retina is the light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye. It contains two types of receptor cells: rods (which detect light intensity and work in dim light) and cones (which detect colour and work in bright light).

questions.stem: What is the function of the iris?

options.text: To control the amount of light entering the eye
To focus light onto the retina
To detect different colours of light
To carry nerve impulses to the brain

questions.explanation: The iris is the coloured part of the eye that controls the size of the pupil, regulating how much light enters the eye. In bright light, the iris makes the pupil smaller; in dim light, it makes the pupil larger.

questions.stem: What is the process by which the lens changes shape to focus on objects at different distances?
questions.explanation: Accommodation is the process by which the ciliary muscles change the shape of the lens to focus on objects at different distances. For near objects the lens becomes fatter (more curved), and for distant objects it becomes thinner (less curved).

questions.stem: When viewing a distant object, what happens to the ciliary muscles and suspensory ligaments?

options.text: Ciliary muscles contract, suspensory ligaments go slack
Ciliary muscles relax, suspensory ligaments pull tight
Ciliary muscles contract, suspensory ligaments pull tight
Ciliary muscles relax, suspensory ligaments go slack

questions.explanation: For distant objects, the ciliary muscles relax, causing the suspensory ligaments to pull tight. This stretches the lens into a thinner shape, which refracts light less to focus the image correctly on the retina.

questions.stem: Which part of the eye refracts (bends) light the most?
questions.explanation: The cornea is responsible for most of the refraction (bending) of light entering the eye. The lens provides additional, adjustable refraction to fine-tune the focus for objects at different distances.

questions.stem: What are rod cells in the retina responsible for?

options.text: Controlling the size of the pupil

questions.explanation: Rod cells are very sensitive to light and work well in dim conditions, but they cannot distinguish colours. They are important for night vision. Cone cells are responsible for detecting colour but need brighter light to function.

questions.stem: Which nerve carries visual information from the eye to the brain?
questions.explanation: The optic nerve carries electrical impulses from the receptor cells in the retina to the brain, where the visual information is processed and interpreted. The point where the optic nerve leaves the eye is called the blind spot.
